name: Oversight Blueprint
summary: House and Senate committees may conduct legislative oversight under separate authorities. The roadmap shows who owns each decision, how to preserve and review evidence, and which actions Congress can take without DOJ. An optional referral requires an independent state-law basis and authorized disclosure. The receiving office decides whether and how to act.
design_premise: Oversight Blueprint assesses that Attorney General Todd Blanche's prior defense of President Donald Trump raises an impartiality concern in matters involving the president. Congress should be able to continue legislative oversight if DOJ does not act.

doj_leadership_context.verified_fact: Todd Blanche is U.S. Attorney General. He previously represented Donald Trump in three criminal cases brought in 2023 and 2024.
doj_leadership_context.referral_boundary: An authorized committee may refer approved evidence when there is an independent state-law basis and a receiving office with jurisdiction. Federal criminal contempt certification under 2 U.S.C. § 194 goes to a U.S. attorney.
